####################################################################################################
Purpose of script: This script prepares the data for models, applying further exclusions based on 
spatial and climate data. The output includes three types of data frames:
####################################################################################################

# Sensitivity analysis with extra methods data =====================================================

# Load packages, themes, directories, and functions
```{r}
rm(list = ls())
source("../00_pck.R")
source("../00_dirs.R")
source("../fun_data/fun_dgsk_modpat.R")
```

# Load the list of data frames per pathogen
```{r}
stu_ppat <- readRDS(glue("{dirs$processed}/stu_ppat.rds"))
# No pertussis combined nor polio combined (as pertussis included dtpa and dtpw and polio ipv and opv)
stu_ppat <- stu_ppat[!(names(stu_ppat) %in% c("pertu", "polio"))]
```

# Data frames for unipathogen models ---------------------------------------------------------------
Prepare data frames for unipathogen models
Unipathogen: Single vaccination with a unique or multiple immunogenicity measurements

# Choosing values for method, serology name, and doses by maximizing total individuals in the methods
# not selected for the main analyses.
```{r}
dat_comb_uni <- list()
# Unipathogen univariate: 
dat_comb_uni$unipat_mono <- lapply(stu_ppat[!str_detect(names(stu_ppat), "7|10|11|13|23")], function(x) {
  # Filter the dataframes to check which combinations have the highest number of individuals
  x %>%
    filter(if_all(starts_with("reg_"), ~ .x >= 0.8)) %>%
    distinct(study, pid, imm_met_s1, imm_sero_s1, doses) %>%
    group_by(imm_met_s1, imm_sero_s1, doses) %>%
    summarise(pid_n = n(), .groups = "drop")
}) %>%
  bind_rows(.id = "pat_dat") %>%
  group_by(pat_dat, imm_sero_s1) %>%
  # Only under primary vaccination
  filter(doses < 4) %>%
  # Select only those with more than one method, and the method that does not have the highest 
  # number of individuals 
  filter(!str_detect(imm_met_s1, imm_met_s1[max(pid_n) == pid_n])) %>%
  # Select now the combination with the highest number of individuals 
  filter(max(pid_n) == pid_n) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  # Label doses and split serology names
  mutate(doses = case_when(pat_dat == "rota" & doses > 1 ~ "l", pat_dat != "rota" & doses == 1 ~ "1", 
                           pat_dat != "rota" & doses == 3 ~ "3"),
         imm_met_s1 = strsplit(imm_met_s1, "-"),
         imm_sero_s1 = strsplit(imm_sero_s1, "-"))

# Unipathogen multivariate 
# Pathogens with multiple seronames: "men" "strep"
dat_comb_uni$unipat_multi <- lapply(stu_ppat[names(stu_ppat) != "strep"], function(x) {
  # Filter the dataframes to check which combinations have the highest number of individuals
  x %>%
    filter(if_all(starts_with("reg_"), ~ .x >= 0.8)) %>%
    distinct(study, pid, imm_met_s1, imm_sero_s1, doses) %>%
    group_by(study, pid, imm_met_s1, doses) %>%
    summarise(imm_sero_s1 = paste(sort(unique(imm_sero_s1)), collapse = "-"), .groups = "drop") %>%
    group_by(imm_met_s1, doses, imm_sero_s1) %>%
    summarise(pid_n = n(), .groups = "drop")
}) %>%
  bind_rows(.id = "pat_dat") %>%
  # Consider only measurement of multiple immunogenicity values  
  filter(str_detect(imm_sero_s1, "-")) %>%
  group_by(pat_dat) %>%
  # Select only those with more than one method, and the method that does not have the highest 
  # number of individuals 
  filter(!str_detect(imm_met_s1, imm_met_s1[max(pid_n) == pid_n])) %>%
  # Select the combination with the highest number of individuals
  filter(max(pid_n) == pid_n) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  # Label doses and split serology names
  mutate(doses = case_when(pat_dat == "rota" & doses > 1 ~ "l", pat_dat != "rota" & doses == 1 ~ "1", 
                           pat_dat != "rota" & doses == 3 ~ "3"),
         imm_met_s1 = strsplit(imm_met_s1, "-"), 
         imm_sero_s1 = strsplit(imm_sero_s1, "-"))

dat_comb_uni <- bind_rows(dat_comb_uni, .id = "multi") %>%
  mutate(prefx = case_when(multi == "unipat_mono" ~ "", .default = "multi_"))
```

# List of data frame combinations
```{r}
dat_select <- dat_comb_uni %>%
  mutate(sufx = case_when(
    multi == "unipat_mono" ~ sub(".*_", "", str_remove_all(imm_sero_s1, "anti_|iga")), 
    .default = ""),
    sufx = case_when(pat_dat == sufx ~ "", .default = sufx)) %>%
  expand_grid(
    multi_pat = FALSE,
    kgc = c(NA, "kgc_1", "kgc_2", "kgc_3"),
    thr = 0.8) %>%
  mutate(name_df = glue(
    "datasemeth_brms_{prefx}{pat_dat}{sufx}_v{doses}_s{str_remove(thr, '\\\\.')}_{kgc}"),
         name_df = str_remove_all(name_df, "_NA"))
```

# Create data frames according to the combinations
```{r}
pat_df_l <- sapply(dat_select$name_df, function(x) {
  
  pat_dat <- if(dat_select[dat_select$name_df == x, "multi"][[1]] == "multipat_multi") { 
    stu_mpat 
  } else { stu_ppat }
  
  # Function to create data frame for mono/multi-pathogen and mono/multivariate models.
  fun_dgsk_modpat(
    dat = pat_dat[[dat_select[dat_select$name_df == x, "pat_dat"][[1]]]], 
    method = dat_select[dat_select$name_df == x, "imm_met_s1"][[1]][[1]],
    seroname = dat_select[dat_select$name_df == x, "imm_sero_s1"][[1]][[1]],
    dose = dat_select[dat_select$name_df == x, "doses"][[1]],
    multi_pat = dat_select[dat_select$name_df == x, "multi_pat"][[1]],
    clim = dat_select[dat_select$name_df == x, "kgc"][[1]],
    clim_thr = dat_select[dat_select$name_df == x, "thr"][[1]])
}, simplify = FALSE)

# Check number of studies and participants
distinct(bind_rows(pat_df_l[str_subset(names(pat_df_l), "kgc", negate = TRUE)]), study)
distinct(bind_rows(pat_df_l[str_subset(names(pat_df_l), "kgc", negate = TRUE)]), study, pid)
length(bind_rows(pat_df_l)$study)

setdiff(distinct(bind_rows(stu_ppat), study)$study,
        distinct(bind_rows(pat_df_l[str_subset(names(pat_df_l), "kgc", negate = TRUE)]), study)$study)
```

# Exclusion per photoperiod and climate group ------------------------------------------------------
```{r}
# Identify groups that ended up with just one observation 
exclude_1obs_df <- sapply(names(pat_df_l), function(i) {
  lapply(c("reg_2", "reg_3", "reg_4", "reg_6", "kgc_1", "kgc_2", "kgc_3"), function(classification) {
    pat_df_l[[i]] %>%
      group_by(!!sym(classification)) %>%
      summarise(count = n()) %>%
      filter(count == 1) %>%
      rename(value = 1) %>%
      mutate(classification = classification) %>%
      select(classification, value, count)}) %>%
    bind_rows()
}, simplify = FALSE) %>%
  bind_rows(.id = "name_df")

# Exclude groups with only one observation based on photoperiod and climate classifications
pat_df_l <- sapply(names(pat_df_l), function(x) {
  # Fetch the corresponding data frame from the list
  data <- pat_df_l[[x]]
  # Fetch rules for the data frame 
  df_rules <- filter(exclude_1obs_df, name_df == x)
  # Apply filtering for each rule in this data frame
  if(nrow(df_rules) > 0) {
    for (i in 1:nrow(df_rules)) {
      classification <- df_rules$classification[i]
      value <- df_rules$value[i]
      # Filter the data frame based on classification and value
      data <- data %>% filter(as.character(!!sym(classification)) != as.character(value))
    }
  }
  return(data)
}, simplify = FALSE)

# Check number of studies and participants
distinct(bind_rows(pat_df_l[str_subset(names(pat_df_l), "kgc", negate = TRUE)]), study)
distinct(bind_rows(pat_df_l[str_subset(names(pat_df_l), "kgc", negate = TRUE)]), study, pid)
length(bind_rows(pat_df_l)$study)
```

# Exclude groups with only one observation per vac_conc and vac_name
```{r}
exclude_1obs_vac_df <- bind_rows(pat_df_l, .id = "name_df") %>%
  group_by(name_df, vac_conc, vac_name_v1) %>%
  summarise(count = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(count == 1) 

pat_df_l <- sapply(names(pat_df_l), function(x) {
  # Fetch the corresponding data frame from the list
  data <- pat_df_l[[x]]
  # Fetch rules for the data frame 
  df_rules <- filter(exclude_1obs_vac_df, name_df == x)
  # Apply filtering for each rule in this data frame
  if(nrow(df_rules) > 0) {
    # Filter the data frame based on classification and value
    data <- data %>% filter(!(vac_conc == df_rules$vac_conc & 
                                vac_name_v1 == as.character(df_rules$vac_name_v1)))
  }
  return(data)
}, simplify = FALSE)
```


# Total participants 
```{r}
lapply(pat_df_l, function(x) c(studies_vl = length(unique(x$study)), 
                               pid_vl = length(unique(x$pid)))) %>%
  bind_rows(.id = "name_df") %>%
  left_join(dat_select, by = join_by(name_df)) %>%
  filter(is.na(kgc)) %>%
  mutate(imm_met_s1 = sapply(imm_met_s1, paste, collapse = ", "),
         imm_sero_s1 = sapply(imm_sero_s1, paste, collapse = ", "))
```

# Save data frames 
```{r}
walk(names(pat_df_l), function(x) {
  pat <- paste0(dat_select[dat_select$name_df == x, "prefx"][[1]], 
                dat_select[dat_select$name_df == x, "pat_dat"][[1]])
  saveRDS(pat_df_l[[x]], glue("{dirs$outputs}/modfit/{x}.rds"))
})
```

# Plot it 
```{r}
bind_rows(pat_df_l[str_subset(names(pat_df_l), "kgc", negate = TRUE)], .id = "dat") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = vac_week_v1, y = reg_6)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.1) + 
  facet_wrap(~dat)
```
